opportunities.evidence: Summer Analyst Intern - Analysis Group Skip to main content Analysis Group is a great place for recent graduates. AG does an incredible job training new hires and preparing them for graduate school. Summer Analyst Intern The summer analyst intern position is an entry-level role that introduces you to the world of economic consulting. Summer analysts work on complex business problems within an inclusive and collaborative environment. They are assigned to work on case teams to experience the role of an analyst, and may work on multiple projects at a time across various practice areas and industries. Generalist analyst interns have opportunities to work on litigation, regulatory, M&A, and other legal-related matters with Analysis Group colleagues, professors from leading institutions, counsel from premier law firms, and corporate and government clients. Health care analyst interns – who are staffed to our HEOR, Epidemiology & Market Access practice – develop experience in life science fields and have opportunities to work closely with our in-house health care experts and with teams from leading pharmaceutical companies. Analysis Group fosters an academically oriented work environment with an emphasis on teamwork and collaboration across multiple areas of expertise. To learn more about the role of a consultant at Analysis Group, visit our What Is Economic Consulting? page. To learn more about the full-time analyst role, please view the Analyst page. Featured Video Watch and learn what it’s like to work as a summer analyst intern at Analysis Group. Candidates We seek students who are enthusiastic about using data and analytics to solve the economic and business challenges facing our clients. They also share in our firm’s dedication to delivering high-quality work through teamwork and collaboration, and nurture our culture of transparency, trust, and respect. Successful summer analyst interns are intellectually curious, have strong interpersonal and communication skills, and enjoy applying quantitative methods to real-world research problems. They also aspire to continuous learning and professional development. We hire two types of summer analyst interns: Generalist interns may work on cases in any of our practice areas. For these internships, we seek rising seniors and first-year master’s students in computer science, economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, or related subjects. Health care interns are staffed to our HEOR, Epidemiology & Market Access practice. This practice seeks interns who are pursuing bachelor’s or master’s degrees in biostatistics, economics, epidemiology, health economics, health policy, mathematics, public health, statistics, or related subjects and are interested in specializing in work related to the life sciences. We invite you to explore the sections below to learn more about summer analyst interns’ responsibilities and opportunities at Analysis Group. Responsibilities Analyzing economic, financial, and health care data Using algorithms and statistical programming in Java, Python, R, SAS, Stata, VBA, and other programs Analyzing data with statistical methods and analytical tools including econometric estimation of models, survival analysis, and machine learning Creating dynamic visualizations to rapidly explore data and models Examining market and industry behavior through targeted research Reviewing and summarizing external reports and client documents Participating in meetings with academic experts and case team members Assisting in the preparation of expert reports and other client deliverables For health care specialists: Conducting a range of health care economics analyses such as treatment patterns and outcomes, comparative effectiveness, cost effectiveness, and budget impact Learning and Development Opportunities Onboarding and Training Programs: Analysis Group offers best-in-class learning opportunities for employees at all levels. We provide summer analyst interns with preparatory training for case work, as well as opportunities to get to know the role of a full-time analyst, learn about the firm, and develop professional relationships. Analytical and Coding Skills Coursework: We provide interns with extensive training in the core analytical skills critical to their case work. This coursework strengthens analysts’ understanding of the firm’s best practices in Excel and in SAS, Stata, R, VBA, and Python coding. Analysis Group University (AGU): Our interns can access our centralized online learning portal and view hundreds of training videos, presentations, and other targeted training content on demand. Technical and nontechnical trainings are available. Summer Programming: Over the course of the experience, the intern cohort attends topical presentations to get to know the firm, how we work, our people, and our practice areas. Analysis Group also hosts senior staff touchpoints so that interns can network with leaders at the firm to learn about their career paths and our culture. Mentorship: Providing a strong support system from day one is very important to us. Interns will have a peer mentor and advisor who will guide them through their summer experience, support them through the onboarding experience, and help them network with individuals outside their case team. Evaluation and Assessment: As they conclude their internships, summer analyst interns are evaluated for the opportunity to return to Analysis Group as full-time analysts. If interns are offered a full-time position and accept, the firm will invest in their professional development and growth, and will provide multidimensional support if they plan to apply to graduate school. Our Staffing Model We choose a case team for every summer analyst intern when they join us. However, our full-time analysts engage in Analysis Group’s internal labor market, which allows them to choose their case work based on their interests. Summer analyst interns may work on multiple cases during their summers with us. You will work with more than just your own cohort at Analysis Group. You will have opportunities to work with other analysts and associates, but you will also interact with senior staff, law firms, industry leaders, and experts within their fields. To learn more about the advancement track at Analysis Group, please visit our Career Path page. To learn about career paths our consultants have taken, please visit the Our People page to read about the personal experiences of Analysis Group consultants and administrative professionals. Case Examples Analyst interns are important contributing members of their teams. Explore our cases to see examples of Analysis Group’s work. If you wish, you can narrow your search by any of our practice areas. Core Values at Analysis Group We believe that a strong and diverse workforce directly supports our goal to provide the highest-quality work, and we are guided in all that we do by principles of fairness, inclusion, and non-discrimination. This drives our commitment to strong talent and business practices that provide rich opportunities to people of all backgrounds. Our collaborative and people- and learning-oriented culture helps our employees contribute fully and meaningfully in the workplace and bring their authentic selves to work each and every day. We have several formal employee-founded and employee-led affinity groups, which are open to all employees and which support equitable and inclusive talent and business practices. Additionally, we are proud to partner with organizations working to enrich and empower the workforce of tomorrow and to expand pathways to opportunity in the economics field. Meet Our Former Analyst Interns Will Celeste Mahir How to Apply Please note that the summer analyst intern role is equivalent to the summer research professional role in Montreal. Please submit your online application, resume, cover letter indicating your geographic preference(s), and unofficial transcript(s) via the Apply button below by the deadline indicated in the relevant job posting. If no deadline is listed, we will review applications on a rolling basis. Apply We welcome your questions. Please feel free to contact us at analyst.recruiter​@​analysisgroup.com . Connect with us on LinkedIn View Our Profile Top Consulting Internship Analysis Group’s summer programs are consistently rated as top consulting internships by Vault. Learn more At Analysis Group, we are committed to providing an accessible workplace and reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, as required by applicable law. We encourage applicants seeking accommodations in the job application process to contact us at +1 617 422 2572 (phone) or at recruitingcompliance@analysisgroup.com for assistance. For more information regarding the rights of U.S.-based applicants and employees, click here . At Analysis Group, we are committed to cybersecurity and to providing a safe experience for job seekers. All official communication regarding employment opportunities will come exclusively via email from the official AnalysisGroup.com domain. We never conduct interviews through texting applications or instant messaging platforms. If you receive an employment offer or other correspondence from an individual at Analysis Group you have not met, or from a non-Analysis Group email domain, it may be a phishing attempt. To ensure online security and protect against potential job scams, please familiarize yourself with the resources available on the Federal Trade Commission’s Job Scams page . Exercise caution and refrain from interacting with unverified domains that are not associated with our official company domain: AnalysisGroup.com . For trustworthy job information about Analysis Group positions, visit https://www.analysisgroup.com/careers/ , and reach out to recruiter@analysisgroup.com if you have any concerns. Together, we can maintain a secure environment and protect against cyber threats.

opportunities.evidence: Students and recent grads - Bank of Canada Skip to content Home Search the site Search FR Change theme Change theme Change theme Change theme Students and recent grads Discover career-launching opportunities designed for students and recent graduates across a wide range of fields. You belong on our team We hire students who are still in school as well as recent graduates and soon-to-be graduates from diverse academic and professional backgrounds. Our solid reputation and exceptional development programs make your professional growth a priority. Working at the Bank of Canada, you will gain real-world experience while building a professional network. Check out our current postings , upload your resume, set job alerts and more. Opportunities for students Scholarships Our Scholarship Award for Post-Secondary Students and Master’s Scholarship Award for women in economics help foster a diverse and talented workforce. These scholarships provide financial assistance to students pursuing post-secondary education. Student work programs We provide hands-on experience through student positions, giving college and university students a chance to contribute meaningfully to our work while receiving mentorship and guidance along the way. Positions are typically for four-month terms . We hire students year-round for these terms: Summer term (May–August): Applications open in January Fall term (September–December): Applications open in May Winter term (January–April): Applications open in August If you are enrolled in a co-op program , before applying you must confirm with your school’s co-op office that our position meets the requirements for your program placement. Governor's Challenge The annual Governor’s Challenge is a university competition puts students in the role of advisor to the Bank’s Governing Council . The aim is to increase students’ understanding of how monetary policy impacts Canada’s economy. Internship opportunities Master’s internships Graduate students studying economics or finance can launch their careers by participating in master’s internships at the Bank. These internships are designed to provide hands-on experience while contributing to both the student’s academic progress and the hiring department’s mandate. This dual focus ensures a beneficial experience for both the student and the organization. Master’s internships are designed to be flexible to accommodate your academic schedule; most terms start in the spring. PhD internships We offer unique opportunities for PhD students specializing in economics, finance or other related fields. As a PhD intern, you will spend two to four months working on your dissertation and presenting and promoting your research at the Bank. You will benefit from a wide range of resources that foster academic and professional success. You will also have the chance to build valuable professional relationships. This includes networking with Bank researchers and engaging with visiting external academics. The experience, exposure and connections you gain during your internship will position you well for future career opportunities. These may include the possibility of a continued role at the Bank. PhD internships are designed to be flexible to accommodate your academic schedule; most terms start in late winter or early spring. Opportunities for recent or soon-to-be graduates Cybersecurity graduates Have you completed a college or university degree in cybersecurity within the past two years? If so, you may be ready to launch your career with an organization at the forefront of cybersecurity innovation. Our cyber team is always looking for emerging talent to help advance our mission to keep Canada’s economy safe and secure. As a recent cybersecurity graduate, you will gain hands-on experience while contributing meaningfully to strengthening the Bank’s security posture. Depending on the role, you may: support security operations analyze cyber threats and events help design and automate security processes enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and readiness optimize security controls across the organization Throughout the program, you will be part of a mission-driven team where your work has a real impact. Your growth and development are a priority. We hire recent cybersecurity graduates year-round, with opportunities posted as they become available. Recruitment campaigns Each year, we invite applications from outstanding recent and soon-to-be graduates in economics and finance. By joining us, you become part of a dynamic community of more than 120 researchers and policy experts with doctoral degrees who drive our mission through innovative research and robust policy analysis. Position start dates can vary depending on the availability of candidates and the hiring teams’ needs. This flexibility allows us to align opportunities with both your schedule and the needs of the Bank. Type of positions we hire for: Research assistants As a research assistant, you will support economists and teams through data analysis and research activities that inform policy-relevant work. Research assistant positions are typically offered for up to two years and provide valuable experience and a solid foundation for future career steps. Participants often go on to pursue graduate education, building on the skills and insights gained during their term at the Bank. Bachelor’s degree candidates (who have graduated in the past two years or are in their final year of study) are eligible to apply for a research assistant position. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in virtual interviews held in November. We run our main recruitment campaigns twice a year, in September and February. If you applied during the fall campaign, there’s no need to apply again to the February posting; your application will automatically be considered part of the winter campaign. Economists and analysts As an economist or analyst, you will use your advanced training in economics or finance to shape analysis and insights that inform research, policy and decisions central to the Bank’s mandate. Master’s degree candidates (who have graduated in the past three years or are in their final year of study) are eligible to apply for a position as an economist or analyst. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in two rounds of interviews in October and November. Senior economists and senior financial sector specialists and analysts As a senior economist or senior financial sector specialist, you will apply deep subject matter expertise and advanced research skills to lead complex analysis, influence policy development, mentor others and contribute expert judgement to advance the Bank’s understanding of key economic and financial system issues. PhD candidates (who have successfully defended their thesis in the past 10 years or who are in the final stages of their degree—near dissertation defense) are eligible to apply for a position as a senior economist or senior financial sector specialist or analyst. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in various rounds of interviews from November through February. Growing in your research career at the Bank Early career development In your initial years, you are expected to develop a research agenda aimed at producing publishable work in leading journals. You will also contribute to analytical work on policy questions. Research plan Leading-edge economic research and analysis is at the heart of policy-making at the Bank. Our researchers develop deep expertise through long-term research and analytical projects on topical policy questions. We seek expertise across a wide range of fields, including: theoretical and applied macroeconomics international macroeconomics and trade international finance and empirical banking banking and payment theory asset pricing econometrics empirical microeconomics industrial organization economic applications of data science Find out more about our current research priorities . Research support and environment The Bank fosters an active and engaged research environment where employees are encouraged to discuss ideas and projects with colleagues and the broader research community. A wide range of resources are available to support research and analytical work. Career paths We are committed to supporting employee growth and development. Clear career paths are outlined in both policy and research streams, and mobility is encouraged between these streams. Employees may pursue either the policy-focused or the research-focused career path. While both groups contribute to policy analysis, those on the research path are expected to maintain an active research agenda targeted at publishing in leading journals. The Bank actively fosters career progression and professional development ensuring employees have opportunities to advance both within their chosen stream and across different roles. Our commitment to mobility allows team members to explore new challenges and grow their expertise, whether they are moving upwards in their current path or transitioning between policy and research streams. This supportive environment empowers our staff to build fulfilling careers while contributing meaningfully to our mission. Find out more Engaging with the research community Collaborating with the research community enriches our understanding and sharpens our policy thinking by bringing in diverse perspectives and advanced research methodologies. We celebrated 10 years of the Governor’s Challenge this year! In the past decade, the Governor’s Challenge has empowered students across Canada to play the part of monetary policy advisors. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. About the team Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data analysts and data scientists learn and grow together. You'll work with some of the most fundamental data at Stripe, and use that data to help drive company-wide initiatives. We have a variety of Data Analytics roles and teams across Stripe and will seek to align you to the most relevant team based on your background. What you’ll do As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling. Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high. Responsibilities Analyze data and running experiments to drive impact Ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly Create metrics, reports, and dashboards to inform and run the business Extend Stripe’s metrics semantic layer Build new data assets and improve existing data assets to support decision-making, products, and business processes Assess the impact of decisions, product launches, and product improvements using business analytics and A/B testing Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns Who you are Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty. Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus. Minimum requirements Enrolled in a quantitative Bachelor’s or Master's degree program (e.g. Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, etc.) with the expectation of graduating in December 2027 or spring/summer 2028 Experience with SQL Proficiency with AI tools to accelerate model development, analysis, and coding Experience communicating and collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a team environment Preferred qualifications Experience writing and debugging data pipelines Demonstrated ability to evaluate and receive feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders via experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects Ability to learn new systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

opportunities.requirements: Join a Challenger At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions. We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences. What's kept us moving? The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward. If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity. We can’t wait to get to know you! We can’t wait to get to know you! Work Term: January - December 2027 This role supports the AI Centre of Enablement in driving enterprise AI adoption and operational excellence. The intern will play a hands-on role in coordinating AI training programs (White Belt, Blue Belt, Black Belt, Executive Belt), managing certification tracking and assignment, organizing training workshops with vendors and internal facilities, and creating and executing internal communication campaigns. This position provides direct exposure to enterprise AI strategy, governance, and change management within a regulated financial services environment. Coordinating end-to-end logistics for AI training programs (White Belt, Blue Belt, Black Belt, Executive Belt), including scheduling, participant tracking, and certificate assignment. Setting up and organizing training workshops with external vendors and internal facilities, including room bookings, calendar invites, and materials preparation. Tracking program enrollment, completion rates, and certification status across all training tiers. Creating and running internal communication campaigns to promote AI training programs, adoption milestones, and enablement resources across channels (e.g., Viva Engage, email, SharePoint). Maintaining and updating AI enablement content on internal SharePoint sites and communication platforms. Supporting the development of training materials, quick reference guides, and promotional assets for AI programs. Assisting with operational processes within the AI Centre of Enablement, including intake tracking, status reporting, and documentation upkeep. Gathering and summarizing feedback from training participants to identify improvement opportunities. Supporting event coordination for AI-related workshops, lunch-and-learns, and community sessions. Currently enrolled in or recently completed a post-secondary program in Business, Communications, Information Technology, Data Analytics, or a related field. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously. Solid written and oral communication skills with the ability to create clear, engaging content for diverse audiences. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 tools (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Excel, PowerPoint). Interest in artificial intelligence, emerging technology, and enterprise digital transformation. Comfort working with data (e.g., tracking spreadsheets, participation dashboards). Self-starter with a proactive attitude and willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment. Experience with graphic design tools (e.g., Canva) or internal communication platforms is considered an asset. Familiarity with the financial services industry is considered an asset. The incumbent will report to the Manager, AI Enablement. The incumbent will work closely with the AI Centre of Enablement team and collaborate with various internal departments (e.g., Learning & Development, Corporate Communications, IT, Operations). The incumbent may interact with external vendors and training partners. Complete responsibilities in a proficient and timely manner. Escalate issues to the Manager, AI Enablement when necessary. Ensure time-sensitive functions such as training session logistics, campaign deadlines, and certificate assignments are completed before deadlines. Will be part of a team focused on scaling AI adoption and literacy across the enterprise. Will be expected to provide feedback and recommendations that could lead to process improvements in enablement operations. What we offer [For full-time permanent roles] 💰 Competitive discretionary bonus ✨ Market leading RRSP match program 🩺  Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits 📝  Employee Share Purchase Plan 👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one 🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days 🖥  Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues 🎓  Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program 💛  A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience Equity, Diversity & Inclusion EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. We provide a barrier‑free recruitment process and work environment. If you require accommodations at any stage, we will work with you to ensure you can bring your best self to the process and beyond. As part of our recruitment process, EQ uses AI to help screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position. All AI-enabled outputs are reviewed and validated by our talent team. All candidates considered for hire must successfully complete a criminal background check and credit check. While we appreciate every application, an EQ recruiter will contact only those whose skills and experience most closely match the requirements of the role. EQB Inc. (TSX: EQB) is the parent company of Equitable Bank, the country's seventh-largest Schedule I bank by assets, which operates EQ Bank, Canada's Challenger Bank™. EQB Inc. serves nearly 4 million Canadians and manages approximately $150 billion in combined assets under management and administration. To learn more, visit eqb.investorroom.com and eqbank.ca .

sources.name: Analysis Group
sources.excerpt: Careers - Analysis Group Skip to main content Once you experience Analysis Group, you will want to work here for the rest of your career. There is no higher praise than that for a workplace. Professional Opportunities Whether you join us as a student or recent graduate or have an established career and significant job experience, we value every member of our diverse, collegial, and international team. Analyst This entry-level position is for undergraduate and graduate students seeking full-time and summer internship opportunities. Full-Time Roles Internships Externships Associate Associates are M.B.A. or Ph.D. holders or candidates, or have a master’s degree and relevant work experience. Full-Time Roles Internships Externships Data Scientists Data scientists help design, implement, and maintain creative solutions to high-profile business, economic, and financial challenges across multiple industries. Learn More Open Roles Administrative Professionals These professionals collaborate with consultants and across teams to support the overall operations of the firm. Learn More Open Roles Your Career at Analysis Group Our firm solves complex business problems in health care, technology, financial services, and other industries. Our consulting teams provide analytical and strategic expertise in engagements with a wide variety of clients. Our consultants and administrative professionals explore and enjoy diverse opportunities. If you join as a consultant, you will work closely with leading professors from our affiliate network to apply academic research to your clients’ challenges, and assist experts on our professional staff who testify in lawsuits. If you join as an administrative professional, you will provide business services essential to the continuing excellence of the firm. You will be a valued member of an Analysis Group team that allows us to maintain our reputation as a top-tier consulting firm and an exceptional place to work. What is Economic Consulting? Why Analysis Group? Rated One of the Best Places to Work The Commonwealth Institute, Glassdoor, Vault, and Management Consulted rate Analysis Group as one of the best places to work. FAQs Get answers to frequently asked questions. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Learn about our commitment to a highly equitable and inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. Pro Bono Learn how our employees apply their expertise to pro bono consulting projects. In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at Analysis Group will be based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. Analysis Group is committed to a policy of non-discrimination and equal opportunity for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, protected veteran status, military service, genetic information, receipt of free medical care, gender identity or expression, family responsibility, familial status, political affiliation, matriculation, place of residence, or any other category protected under applicable law. Analysis Group will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law. This commitment is evident in all aspects of Analysis Group’s employment practices and policies, including recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, discipline, discharge, benefits, and training. If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click here . At Analysis Group, we are committed to cybersecurity and to providing a safe experience for job seekers. All official communication regarding employment opportunities will come exclusively via email from the official AnalysisGroup.com domain. We never conduct interviews through texting applications or instant messaging platforms. If you receive an employment offer or other correspondence from an individual at Analysis Group you have not met, or from a non-Analysis Group email domain, it may be a phishing attempt. To ensure online security and protect against potential job scams, please familiarize yourself with the resources available on the Federal Trade Commission’s Job Scams page . Exercise caution and refrain from interacting with unverified domains that are not associated with our official company domain: AnalysisGroup.com . For trustworthy job information about Analysis Group positions, visit https://www.analysisgroup.com/careers/ , and reach out to recruiter@analysisgroup.com if you have any concerns. Together, we can maintain a secure environment and protect against cyber threats.

sources.name: NERA
sources.excerpt: Why NERA Skip to main content Careers: Why NERA NERA experts come from a variety of professional backgrounds—including academia, government, regulatory agencies, accounting, and law—bringing with them distinctive ideas, perspectives, and expertise. Our culture is one of collaboration, development, and a hands-on approach to consulting. Why NERA Life at NERA Career Path Open Roles Recruiting Events HELP COMPANIES, MARKETS, AND GOVERNMENTS MEET THEIR HARDEST CHALLENGES WITH THE BEST ECONOMIC GUIDANCE. Competition, regulation, public policy, strategy, finance, and litigation are high-stakes and high-pressure matters with billions of dollars on the line. We provide the proof-positive businesses, policymakers, regulators, and judges need to make their most important decisions—decisions they can trust and by which others will abide. play AWARDS Our Work At NERA, you’ll use customized analytical approaches and develop innovative solutions to get to the truth behind future-making matters and deliver unbiased and defensible findings. You’ll take a multidisciplinary approach that includes applying economic theory and your skills in statistics, econometrics, finance, game theory, mathematics, and computer science to the most challenging issues our clients face. Those issues span everything from the valuation of corporate guarantees and assessing healthcare company mergers to designing competitive energy markets and informing international tax policy. “The team gets to hear directly how the expert is thinking about a report, how to defend the opinions, how to anticipate critiques. The NERA team is always much closer to a case than at other firms.” —Managing Director, New York Our Path to Success Succeeding at NERA means you’re intellectually curious. You are excited about the real-world challenges you’re working on, you love to learn, and you’re interested in solving complex problems through analysis and data synthesis. You are also a team player who takes initiative, asks questions, and takes responsibility for your work. You approach problems methodically, paying close attention to detail and developing accurate and objective conclusions. Strong communication skills are a must, and a passion for economics doesn’t hurt, either. “It’s a privilege to be in a position where we’re in the business of helping sift through a gray, complex environment to find truth where there is no black and white. I think that is really rewarding.” —Senior Analyst, Washington, DC Our Organization NERA is composed of teams led by in-house experts. As a team member, you’ll work directly with leading economic experts and practitioners as well as our external academic affiliates. Our leaders provide guidance and mentorship, give team members a voice in high-stakes matters, and foster relationships and trust with colleagues across sectors and seniority. NERA places the utmost importance on collegiality, prioritizing your professional success, providing actionable feedback, and investing in your professional growth and technical expertise. “NERA rewards entrepreneurship and taking initiative. We invest heavily in the professional development of our staff because we want to cultivate people who can become successful experts in their own right.” —Managing Director, New York Join Us in Delivering Economic Excellence Worldwide Because NERA is part of Marsh, during the application process you will be directed to the Marsh job search site. sources.excerpt: Careers | Brattle Intellectual curiosity, a passion for principles, a strong team orientation, and respect for clients and colleagues are part of the Brattle DNA. We’re always seeking bright, collaborative professionals to join our team. As a growing firm with offices in major metropolitan centers in North America, Europe, and Australia, we seek bright, energetic professionals looking for intellectual challenges to join our team. Because our firm’s success derives from the quality of our people, we are committed to each individual’s personal and professional development and success. Clients rely upon experts at The Brattle Group to solve their most challenging problems. Our experts offer sophisticated capabilities in economic modeling, econometrics, and financial analysis, and we have appeared before courts, governments, and arbitration panels around the world. If you share our core values, and are seeking a stimulating, collegial, and fun environment in which to pursue your career, we invite you to learn more about what makes Brattle such a great place to work. To view our Equal Opportunity Employer Statement, click here . Corporate Citizenship Careers Navigation Overview Why Brattle? Belonging at Brattle Benefits Our Work Roles Current Openings Recruiting Events Learning & Development Life Beyond Brattle FAQs For more than three decades, Brattle has been a place where people grow, careers flourish, relationships develop, and collaboration drives results. As a privately held firm, we take the long view, investing in all employees, giving back through meaningful pro bono work, and pursuing groundbreaking cases and mission-driven work. Our culture is rooted in four Foundational Principles: development, collegiality, quality, and sustainability. These values are our “True North” – guiding our approach to client service, working together, and firm decision-making. Development Developing our people, with a focus on being an inter-generational firm and believing that everyone can be an owner and an entrepreneurial consultant. Collegiality Being good colleagues by being collaborative, building and valuing trusting relationships, being jointly responsible for the firm’s governance and management, and striving to be an inclusive and equitable firm focused on fostering diversity. Quality Ensuring our work and actions build and sustain a culture and reputation for high quality. Quality is broader than just getting the economics right, and includes a commitment to optimizing the experience for our internal and external clients. While quality does not necessarily differentiate us within our metrics, it is so foundational that we also include it here. Sustainability Having a shared understanding that while both long-term profitability and growth are necessary to support development opportunities and to attract, retain, develop, and support top talent, neither is our primary goal. We prioritize development and colleagueship over short-term profit motives. Why Brattle? What makes Brattle a great place to work and grow professionally? From interesting people to the challenging work, it’s a combination of factors that together create an outstanding work environment. How to hire a French-speaking or bilingual foreign worker to work in Canada outside Quebec - Canada.ca How to hire a French-speaking or bilingual foreign worker to work in Canada outside Quebec Step 1. Find a candidate and make sure they’re eligible Find out what options you have to find a French-speaking or bilingual worker . Candidates must be eligible to apply for a Francophone Mobility work permit. Make sure you know the requirements before hiring. If the candidate is applying for the work permit on or after June 15, 2023 To be eligible, the candidate must meet the general eligibility requirements for a work permit choose to live and work in 1 of the 9 Canadian provinces or 3 territories outside Quebec be able to prove they can speak and listen in French at an intermediate level This would be equivalent to a niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) level 5 or higher. have an offer of employment for a job that’s classified under any Training, Education, Experience and Responsibilities category of the National Occupational Classification (NOC) system except if the offer of employment is for a job in a primary agriculture occupation under TEER 4 and 5 If the candidate applied for the work permit before June 15, 2023 To be eligible, the worker must have met the general eligibility requirements for a work permit chosen to live and work in 1 of the 9 Canadian provinces or 3 territories outside Quebec been able to satisfy a processing officer that they could score a minimum of 7 on the niveaux de compétence linguistique canadiens (NCLC) test had an offer of employment for a job that’s classified under a TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 category of the NOC Step 2. Submit an offer of employment If the French-speaking or bilingual foreign candidate you want to hire meets the eligibility requirements above, you can hire them without an LMIA. 
  To do this, you must sign in or create an account in the Employer Portal submit an offer of employment through the Employer Portal using LMIA exemption code C16 for Mobilité Francophone pay a $230 employer compliance fee Step 3. Provide your candidate with the information they need to apply Once you submit an offer of employment, you need to provide your candidate with their offer of employment number: a 7-digit number they will require for their application the signed offer of employment Once you complete the steps above, the candidate can apply for their work permit. Make sure they submit their work permit application through Francophone Mobility . Find out more about hiring without an LMIA . Supporting your worker’s permanent residence Learn about how you can help the hired foreign worker stay in Canada permanently . Page details 2026-04-28

sources.excerpt: Summer Analyst Intern - Analysis Group Skip to main content Analysis Group is a great place for recent graduates. AG does an incredible job training new hires and preparing them for graduate school. Summer Analyst Intern The summer analyst intern position is an entry-level role that introduces you to the world of economic consulting. Summer analysts work on complex business problems within an inclusive and collaborative environment. They are assigned to work on case teams to experience the role of an analyst, and may work on multiple projects at a time across various practice areas and industries. Generalist analyst interns have opportunities to work on litigation, regulatory, M&A, and other legal-related matters with Analysis Group colleagues, professors from leading institutions, counsel from premier law firms, and corporate and government clients. Health care analyst interns – who are staffed to our HEOR, Epidemiology & Market Access practice – develop experience in life science fields and have opportunities to work closely with our in-house health care experts and with teams from leading pharmaceutical companies. Analysis Group fosters an academically oriented work environment with an emphasis on teamwork and collaboration across multiple areas of expertise. To learn more about the role of a consultant at Analysis Group, visit our What Is Economic Consulting? page. To learn more about the full-time analyst role, please view the Analyst page. Featured Video Watch and learn what it’s like to work as a summer analyst intern at Analysis Group. Candidates We seek students who are enthusiastic about using data and analytics to solve the economic and business challenges facing our clients. They also share in our firm’s dedication to delivering high-quality work through teamwork and collaboration, and nurture our culture of transparency, trust, and respect. Successful summer analyst interns are intellectually curious, have strong interpersonal and communication skills, and enjoy applying quantitative methods to real-world research problems. They also aspire to continuous learning and professional development. We hire two types of summer analyst interns: Generalist interns may work on cases in any of our practice areas. For these internships, we seek rising seniors and first-year master’s students in computer science, economics, finance, mathematics, statistics, or related subjects. Health care interns are staffed to our HEOR, Epidemiology & Market Access practice. This practice seeks interns who are pursuing bachelor’s or master’s degrees in biostatistics, economics, epidemiology, health economics, health policy, mathematics, public health, statistics, or related subjects and are interested in specializing in work related to the life sciences. We invite you to explore the sections below to learn more about summer analyst interns’ responsibilities and opportunities at Analysis Group. Responsibilities Analyzing economic, financial, and health care data Using algorithms and statistical programming in Java, Python, R, SAS, Stata, VBA, and other programs Analyzing data with statistical methods and analytical tools including econometric estimation of models, survival analysis, and machine learning Creating dynamic visualizations to rapidly explore data and models Examining market and industry behavior through targeted research Reviewing and summarizing external reports and client documents Participating in meetings with academic experts and case team members Assisting in the preparation of expert reports and other client deliverables For health care specialists: Conducting a range of health care economics analyses such as treatment patterns and outcomes, comparative effectiveness, cost effectiveness, and budget impact Learning and Development Opportunities Onboarding and Training Programs: Analysis Group offers best-in-class learning opportunities for employees at all levels. We provide summer analyst interns with preparatory training for case work, as well as opportunities to get to know the role of a full-time analyst, learn about the firm, and develop professional relationships. Analytical and Coding Skills Coursework: We provide interns with extensive training in the core analytical skills critical to their case work. This coursework strengthens analysts’ understanding of the firm’s best practices in Excel and in SAS, Stata, R, VBA, and Python coding. Analysis Group University (AGU): Our interns can access our centralized online learning portal and view hundreds of training videos, presentations, and other targeted training content on demand. Technical and nontechnical trainings are available. Summer Programming: Over the course of the experience, the intern cohort attends topical presentations to get to know the firm, how we work, our people, and our practice areas. Analysis Group also hosts senior staff touchpoints so that interns can network with leaders at the firm to learn about their career paths and our culture. Mentorship: Providing a strong support system from day one is very important to us. Interns will have a peer mentor and advisor who will guide them through their summer experience, support them through the onboarding experience, and help them network with individuals outside their case team. Evaluation and Assessment: As they conclude their internships, summer analyst interns are evaluated for the opportunity to return to Analysis Group as full-time analysts. If interns are offered a full-time position and accept, the firm will invest in their professional development and growth, and will provide multidimensional support if they plan to apply to graduate school. Our Staffing Model We choose a case team for every summer analyst intern when they join us. However, our full-time analysts engage in Analysis Group’s internal labor market, which allows them to choose their case work based on their interests. Summer analyst interns may work on multiple cases during their summers with us. You will work with more than just your own cohort at Analysis Group. You will have opportunities to work with other analysts and associates, but you will also interact with senior staff, law firms, industry leaders, and experts within their fields. To learn more about the advancement track at Analysis Group, please visit our Career Path page. To learn about career paths our consultants have taken, please visit the Our People page to read about the personal experiences of Analysis Group consultants and administrative professionals. Case Examples Analyst interns are important contributing members of their teams. Explore our cases to see examples of Analysis Group’s work. If you wish, you can narrow your search by any of our practice areas. Core Values at Analysis Group We believe that a strong and diverse workforce directly supports our goal to provide the highest-quality work, and we are guided in all that we do by principles of fairness, inclusion, and non-discrimination. This drives our commitment to strong talent and business practices that provide rich opportunities to people of all backgrounds. Our collaborative and people- and learning-oriented culture helps our employees contribute fully and meaningfully in the workplace and bring their authentic selves to work each and every day. We have several formal employee-founded and employee-led affinity groups, which are open to all employees and which support equitable and inclusive talent and business practices. Additionally, we are proud to partner with organizations working to enrich and empower the workforce of tomorrow and to expand pathways to opportunity in the economics field. Meet Our Former Analyst Interns Will Celeste Mahir How to Apply Please note that the summer analyst intern role is equivalent to the summer research professional role in Montreal. Please submit your online application, resume, cover letter indicating your geographic preference(s), and unofficial transcript(s) via the Apply button below by the deadline indicated in the relevant job posting. If no deadline is listed, we will review applications on a rolling basis. Apply We welcome your questions. Please feel free to contact us at analyst.recruiter​@​analysisgroup.com . Connect with us on LinkedIn View Our Profile Top Consulting Internship Analysis Group’s summer programs are consistently rated as top consulting internships by Vault. Learn more At Analysis Group, we are committed to providing an accessible workplace and reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, as required by applicable law. We encourage applicants seeking accommodations in the job application process to contact us at +1 617 422 2572 (phone) or at recruitingcompliance@analysisgroup.com for assistance. For more information regarding the rights of U.S.-based applicants and employees, click here . At Analysis Group, we are committed to cybersecurity and to providing a safe experience for job seekers. All official communication regarding employment opportunities will come exclusively via email from the official AnalysisGroup.com domain. We never conduct interviews through texting applications or instant messaging platforms. If you receive an employment offer or other correspondence from an individual at Analysis Group you have not met, or from a non-Analysis Group email domain, it may be a phishing attempt. To ensure online security and protect against potential job scams, please familiarize yourself with the resources available on the Federal Trade Commission’s Job Scams page . Exercise caution and refrain from interacting with unverified domains that are not associated with our official company domain: AnalysisGroup.com . For trustworthy job information about Analysis Group positions, visit https://www.analysisgroup.com/careers/ , and reach out to recruiter@analysisgroup.com if you have any concerns. Together, we can maintain a secure environment and protect against cyber threats.

sources.excerpt: Students and recent grads - Bank of Canada Skip to content Home Search the site Search FR Change theme Change theme Change theme Change theme Students and recent grads Discover career-launching opportunities designed for students and recent graduates across a wide range of fields. You belong on our team We hire students who are still in school as well as recent graduates and soon-to-be graduates from diverse academic and professional backgrounds. Our solid reputation and exceptional development programs make your professional growth a priority. Working at the Bank of Canada, you will gain real-world experience while building a professional network. Check out our current postings , upload your resume, set job alerts and more. Opportunities for students Scholarships Our Scholarship Award for Post-Secondary Students and Master’s Scholarship Award for women in economics help foster a diverse and talented workforce. These scholarships provide financial assistance to students pursuing post-secondary education. Student work programs We provide hands-on experience through student positions, giving college and university students a chance to contribute meaningfully to our work while receiving mentorship and guidance along the way. Positions are typically for four-month terms . We hire students year-round for these terms: Summer term (May–August): Applications open in January Fall term (September–December): Applications open in May Winter term (January–April): Applications open in August If you are enrolled in a co-op program , before applying you must confirm with your school’s co-op office that our position meets the requirements for your program placement. Governor's Challenge The annual Governor’s Challenge is a university competition puts students in the role of advisor to the Bank’s Governing Council . The aim is to increase students’ understanding of how monetary policy impacts Canada’s economy. Internship opportunities Master’s internships Graduate students studying economics or finance can launch their careers by participating in master’s internships at the Bank. These internships are designed to provide hands-on experience while contributing to both the student’s academic progress and the hiring department’s mandate. This dual focus ensures a beneficial experience for both the student and the organization. Master’s internships are designed to be flexible to accommodate your academic schedule; most terms start in the spring. PhD internships We offer unique opportunities for PhD students specializing in economics, finance or other related fields. As a PhD intern, you will spend two to four months working on your dissertation and presenting and promoting your research at the Bank. You will benefit from a wide range of resources that foster academic and professional success. You will also have the chance to build valuable professional relationships. This includes networking with Bank researchers and engaging with visiting external academics. The experience, exposure and connections you gain during your internship will position you well for future career opportunities. These may include the possibility of a continued role at the Bank. PhD internships are designed to be flexible to accommodate your academic schedule; most terms start in late winter or early spring. Opportunities for recent or soon-to-be graduates Cybersecurity graduates Have you completed a college or university degree in cybersecurity within the past two years? If so, you may be ready to launch your career with an organization at the forefront of cybersecurity innovation. Our cyber team is always looking for emerging talent to help advance our mission to keep Canada’s economy safe and secure. As a recent cybersecurity graduate, you will gain hands-on experience while contributing meaningfully to strengthening the Bank’s security posture. Depending on the role, you may: support security operations analyze cyber threats and events help design and automate security processes enhance employee cybersecurity awareness and readiness optimize security controls across the organization Throughout the program, you will be part of a mission-driven team where your work has a real impact. Your growth and development are a priority. We hire recent cybersecurity graduates year-round, with opportunities posted as they become available. Recruitment campaigns Each year, we invite applications from outstanding recent and soon-to-be graduates in economics and finance. By joining us, you become part of a dynamic community of more than 120 researchers and policy experts with doctoral degrees who drive our mission through innovative research and robust policy analysis. Position start dates can vary depending on the availability of candidates and the hiring teams’ needs. This flexibility allows us to align opportunities with both your schedule and the needs of the Bank. Type of positions we hire for: Research assistants As a research assistant, you will support economists and teams through data analysis and research activities that inform policy-relevant work. Research assistant positions are typically offered for up to two years and provide valuable experience and a solid foundation for future career steps. Participants often go on to pursue graduate education, building on the skills and insights gained during their term at the Bank. Bachelor’s degree candidates (who have graduated in the past two years or are in their final year of study) are eligible to apply for a research assistant position. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in virtual interviews held in November. We run our main recruitment campaigns twice a year, in September and February. If you applied during the fall campaign, there’s no need to apply again to the February posting; your application will automatically be considered part of the winter campaign. Economists and analysts As an economist or analyst, you will use your advanced training in economics or finance to shape analysis and insights that inform research, policy and decisions central to the Bank’s mandate. Master’s degree candidates (who have graduated in the past three years or are in their final year of study) are eligible to apply for a position as an economist or analyst. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in two rounds of interviews in October and November. Senior economists and senior financial sector specialists and analysts As a senior economist or senior financial sector specialist, you will apply deep subject matter expertise and advanced research skills to lead complex analysis, influence policy development, mentor others and contribute expert judgement to advance the Bank’s understanding of key economic and financial system issues. PhD candidates (who have successfully defended their thesis in the past 10 years or who are in the final stages of their degree—near dissertation defense) are eligible to apply for a position as a senior economist or senior financial sector specialist or analyst. Selected individuals will be invited to participate in various rounds of interviews from November through February. Growing in your research career at the Bank Early career development In your initial years, you are expected to develop a research agenda aimed at producing publishable work in leading journals. You will also contribute to analytical work on policy questions. Research plan Leading-edge economic research and analysis is at the heart of policy-making at the Bank. Our researchers develop deep expertise through long-term research and analytical projects on topical policy questions. We seek expertise across a wide range of fields, including: theoretical and applied macroeconomics international macroeconomics and trade international finance and empirical banking banking and payment theory asset pricing econometrics empirical microeconomics industrial organization economic applications of data science Find out more about our current research priorities . Research support and environment The Bank fosters an active and engaged research environment where employees are encouraged to discuss ideas and projects with colleagues and the broader research community. A wide range of resources are available to support research and analytical work. Career paths We are committed to supporting employee growth and development. Clear career paths are outlined in both policy and research streams, and mobility is encouraged between these streams. Employees may pursue either the policy-focused or the research-focused career path. While both groups contribute to policy analysis, those on the research path are expected to maintain an active research agenda targeted at publishing in leading journals. The Bank actively fosters career progression and professional development ensuring employees have opportunities to advance both within their chosen stream and across different roles. Our commitment to mobility allows team members to explore new challenges and grow their expertise, whether they are moving upwards in their current path or transitioning between policy and research streams. This supportive environment empowers our staff to build fulfilling careers while contributing meaningfully to our mission. Find out more Engaging with the research community Collaborating with the research community enriches our understanding and sharpens our policy thinking by bringing in diverse perspectives and advanced research methodologies. We celebrated 10 years of the Governor’s Challenge this year! In the past decade, the Governor’s Challenge has empowered students across Canada to play the part of monetary policy advisors.  Partner with TWS and business stakeholders to identify, assess, prioritize, and document high-value AI, automation, and process-improvement opportunities. 
 Analyze current-state workflows, pain points, controls, dependencies, exception paths, data requirements, and measurable improvement objectives. 
 Determine whether AI, workflow automation, scripting, process redesign, or a non-technical change is the most appropriate response to a business or operational need. 
 Translate business requirements into process designs, solution requirements, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, implementation plans, support models, and measurable success criteria. 
 Develop use cases for ticket summarization, triage, routing, response drafting, knowledge retrieval, trend analysis, and service-quality checks. 
 Maintain a prioritized AI and automation pipeline aligned with TWS objectives, capacity, risk tolerance, and measurable business value. 
 Gather user feedback, identify adoption barriers, and recommend process or solution improvements that increase usability and sustained value. 

 AI Engineering & Solution Development (40%) 

 Design, configure, develop, test, deploy, maintain, and support secure, scalable, and maintainable AI-powered copilots, agents, automations, scripts, analytics, and low-code solutions for TWS and digital workplace use cases. 
 Build proof-of-concepts, prototypes, and production-ready solutions using approved platforms such as Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform, APIs, PowerShell, Python, and other sanctioned technologies. 
 Develop enterprise search, retrieval, grounding, orchestration, agent, and workflow solutions using approved TWS and enterprise knowledge sources. 
 Create reusable prompts, workflows, templates, connectors, scripts, integrations, and solution components to improve consistency and accelerate delivery. 
 Integrate AI capabilities with Microsoft 365, ServiceNow, HR platforms, collaboration tools, endpoint, asset, identity, reporting, knowledge, and operational workflow systems. 
 Define grounding sources, data mappings, permission boundaries, validation rules, structured outputs, and controls so solutions are accurate, traceable, and fit for purpose. 
 Apply approved engineering practices for environment management, configuration, credentials, source control, testing, release, monitoring, logging, troubleshooting, recovery, rollback, and retirement. 
 Complete functional, security, privacy, accessibility, regression, and user acceptance testing before production release. 
 Create and maintain technical runbooks covering ownership, dependencies, access, recovery, rollback, incident response, monitoring, support handoff, and retirement. 
 Collaborate with Architecture, Security, Privacy, Risk, Service Management, Data, platform teams, and vendors to validate designs and address gaps before implementation. 

 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Use (15%) 

 Ensure AI and automation solutions comply with approved architecture, security, privacy, data governance, records-management, acceptable-use, change-management, audit, accessibility, and regulatory requirements. 
 Perform preliminary risk and impact assessments and engage Information Security, Privacy, Risk, Compliance, Data, Architecture, or other control partners as required. 
 Implement responsible AI controls, including access management, data protection, auditability, output validation, exception handling, escalation, rollback, and human oversight. 
 Document solution purpose, users, data inputs, processing logic, outputs, limitations, risks, dependencies, controls, approvals, testing, changes, exceptions, incidents, and periodic reviews. 
 Ensure AI-generated outputs and automated actions are validated and are not used as the sole basis for material operational or access decisions. 
 Escalate material risks, control failures, data exposure, inaccurate outcomes, production issues, and high-priority service impacts to the Manager, TWS and appropriate partners. 

 Knowledge Management, Adoption & Continuous Improvement (5%) 

 Develop and maintain AI-assisted knowledge articles, SOPs, troubleshooting guides, prompt guidance, playbooks, standards, reference architectures, job aids, and support documentation. 
 Validate AI-assisted content for accuracy, clarity, accessibility, currency, and alignment with approved processes before publication. 
 Build AI literacy and adoption through demonstrations, workshops, training, coaching, knowledge sharing, enablement programs, and office-hour support. 
 Advise teams on AI best practices, prompt engineering, output validation, data handling, responsible use, solution design, and automation opportunities. 
 Monitor solution accuracy, reliability, security, privacy, cost efficiency, adoption, exceptions, user satisfaction, and business outcomes; implement improvements based on evidence and feedback. 
 Develop dashboards, metrics, and reporting that demonstrate adoption, quality, productivity gains, automation savings, service improvements, risk reduction, and operational impact. 

 Technology Workplace Services Technology Support & Operational Continuity (10%) 

 Provide targeted support for endpoints, collaboration tools, audio/visual equipment, enterprise applications, and related workplace technology services when required. 
 Use operational knowledge to validate that AI-enabled improvements function effectively within TWS support processes and meet user needs. 
 Manage assigned incidents, requests, problems, and changes in accordance with ITIL practices, documented procedures, service expectations, and escalation requirements. 
 Assist with onboarding, offboarding, device deployment, software rollout, inventory, and other TWS activities during priority events or coverage needs. 
 Monitor and respond to production issues affecting AI-enabled workflows, automations, or related TWS services. 

 "},{"text":"Let's Talk About You! ","content":" 

 College diploma or university degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Technology, Data and Analytics, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience. 
 5 or more years of experience in IT service delivery, workplace technology, AI enablement, process improvement, automation, business analysis, or a related technical role. 
 Practical experience analyzing requirements and designing, documenting, testing, deploying, monitoring, and supporting AI, automation, scripting, analytics, or low-code solutions. 
 Working knowledge of generative AI and solution patterns, including prompt design and orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, enterprise search, grounding, structured output, tool or function calling, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop controls. 
 Familiarity with Microsoft 365 and approved enterprise AI and automation platforms, including Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Azure AI, PowerShell, APIs, and related tools used by the Bank. 
 Knowledge of API integration, authentication and authorization, managed identities or service accounts, secrets management, data transformation, secure connector design, source control, solution packaging, environment configuration, release management, monitoring, logging, and technical runbooks. 
 Understanding of ITIL practices, including Incident, Request, Problem, Change, Knowledge, Asset, and Service Level Management. 
 Strong knowledge of security, privacy, data lifecycle, governance, classification, minimization, access, retention, lineage, appropriate use, and AI evaluation principles. 
 Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, communication, collaboration, prioritization, and change-adoption skills, with the ability to evaluate effort, dependencies, risk, business value, and technical trade-offs. 
 Commitment to continuous learning as AI technologies, engineering practices, security expectations, and regulatory requirements evolve.

The role plays a key part in strengthening enterprise ￼ wide consistency, transparency, and governance of lending risk by providing timely, data ￼ driven insights to Risk leadership.

 ","id":"bf8ef8f5-db0e-40d2-a3a5-b8836bf1a22e","lists":[{"text":"The Core Responsibilities","content":" 
 
 
 Lending Portfolio Analytics & Tier Oversight 
 
 
 
 
 Analyze lending portfolios segmented by geographic region, on an ongoing basis, including monitoring lending tiers and related risk indicators. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Assess portfolio performance trends, concentrations, and emerging risks, including analysis of internal credit risk indicators (e.g., delinquencies, loan-to-value, impairments) to evaluate portfolio risk dynamics. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Monitor and analyze macroeconomic and regional factors (e.g., house price index, employment growth, demographic, occupational shifts, and economic conditions) through review of industry publications, economic reports, and relevant news sources to assess their impact on lending portfolio risk and tiering assumptions. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Identify variances, anomalous trends, early warning indicators, or signs of portfolio drift, perform root cause analysis, and escalate findings through established Credit Risk channels. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Lead periodic review and validation of lending tiers and segmentation methodologies, including recommending tier upgrades/downgrades based on analytical insights and observed risk outcomes. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Risk Reporting & Management Insights 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare recurring and ad-hoc reports and dashboards on lending portfolio performance, regional trends, and key risk metrics, delivering clear, timely insights to Risk leadership and stakeholders. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Support the development of executive ‑ ready materials to inform Risk leadership and senior stakeholders. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of data used in analytics and reporting outputs. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Stakeholder Collaboration & Governance Support 
 
 
 
 
 Partner with first ‑ line lending, credit, and business teams to validate data inputs, clarify assumptions, and gather insights on emerging industry trends and market developments to inform portfolio analytics and risk assessment. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Provide independent challenge and recommend tiering updates (including upgrades/downgrades) where appropriate to ensure alignment with Risk appetite and governance expectations. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Act as a Risk point of contact for analytical inquiries related to lending portfolios and tiering. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Contribute documentation and analysis required for internal reviews, audits, or regulatory requests related to lending portfolio risk and governance. 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Continuous Improvement & AI Enablement 
 
 
 
 
 Identify opportunities to improve analytical processes, controls, and data quality related to lending portfolio analytics. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Support automation, standardization, and reporting enhancements, including the use of AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot Studio. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Design, build, and maintain agentic workflows and automations using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate to streamline repetitive analytical, reporting, and data-quality tasks and improve the scalability of lending portfolio analytics. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Apply emerging AI and automation capabilities responsibly, ensuring alignment with the Bank's risk, governance, data, and model risk controls. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Contribute to broader risk transformation initiatives that strengthen analytical capability and scalability across the Risk function. 
 

 
 
 "},{"text":"Let's Talk About You","content":" 
 
 
 
 Undergraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Data Analytics, or a related discipline (or equivalent combination of education and experience). 
 

 
 
 
 
 Typically 1–3 years of progressive experience in risk analytics, portfolio analytics, credit analytics, or a related analytical role. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Strong analytical and problem ‑ solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex datasets and translate insights into clear findings. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience working with reporting, visualization, or analytics tools (e.g., Power BI); experience in a regulated financial services environment is an asset. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Proficiency in SQL for data extraction, querying, and filtering large datasets to support portfolio analysis and reporting. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Strong business and risk acumen, including understanding of residential mortgage lending and credit risk terminology and key risk drivers (e.g., loan-to-value, arrears, delinquency, total /gross debt service ratio, probability of default, exposure at default, loss given default) to support effective analysis and interpretation of portfolio performance. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Strong attention to detail and demonstrated commitment to data accuracy and integrity. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present analytical insights to non ‑ technical stakeholders. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Ability to manage competing priorities in a deadline ‑ driven environment with appropriate guidance and supervision. 
 

 
 
 
 
 Familiarity with AI-assisted analytics or low-code automation tools such as Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate, and an interest in building agentic workflows to streamline analytical and reporting tasks, is an asset.

At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.
 
With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
 
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Remote Roles: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.
 
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field.
Sufficient familiarity with Azure Machine Learning components, Databricks processing and serverless environments, and ML Frameworks to support strategic decision making
